I love/d ToS, but the devs ruined this. Such a waste.

Here's what I wish I could say.

This is a love letter of a game.
A beautiful spiritual successor to Ragnarok Online with unique, interesting classes, and rewarding addictive gameplay.

But the truth here is, I came back because for some reason the reviews are now trending positive on this game.
But reading them, I see many of the same issues that plagued it before haven't been resolved.
Devs don't care.
The community is long since dead.

Which is a damn shame.
Because it has the potential to be one of the greats.

Years and years ago I could NOT stop playing this game.
I've logged close to 1200 hours.
This is easily more than 10x the closest contender in my steam library.

Despite all it's major flaws, and dumb p2w mechanics, there was something truly special about the ToS community.
It was exhilarating rolling with a crew of homies and just DECIMATING a dungeon together.
But then folks started leaving.
Trickling away.

And the only ones left were just hardcore end gamers.

It became impossible to start up a new character because you needed new folks to run entry level dungeons together.
New content meant old build viability went out the window, and you just had to grind up a brand new character to make it work because now that beloved character that you carefully researched for hours to min/max was totally useless.

It's hard to know what to say here.
I had a lot of good times playing this game.
I made real friends.
I have fond memories and bittersweet ones too.
I'm glad for the time I spent playing it.

But I wish the Devs had taken a little more time to make this is better experience for us as players.
There were some glaring flaws in game progression that they never addressed, even though they (still) run a weekly maintenance.
Instead it seems like they chose to squeeze as much money out as they possibly could before the ship sank.

It was fun while it lasted.
I miss playing.

I would have loved to add a ton more, but this is the limit I can.

[h1]PROS:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Extremely diverse class system. Many different ways to build your character, but limited (Reason in cons).
[*]Huge map to explore.
[*]Many levels giving it an interesting goal to get to cap. Current cap at this time is upwards of nearly 300 levels.
[*]Many items to gear your character. Most classes can go 1h + offhand/shield or 2handed weapon allowing you to go tanky or focus dps.
[*]You generate TP (In-game Cash Shop currency) overtime, to a maximum of 5 TP. You can use this to get several items which includes Megaphones to use global chat (or shout chat for this game.
[*]Cosmetics can have stat improvements to buff your character. (Con below to go with this.)
[*]Collections are rewarding by giving you bonus' for completing them. These bonus' are also carried across your entire Team (family/characters). (Con below to go with this.)
[*]Fairly large storage which can be upgraded is a nice change from games which only allow 10-20 items to be stored.
[*]Upgrading gear isn't NEARLY as challenging as some other games making it nice to be able to upgrade gear. Your "fail chance" never drops below 51%.
[/list]

I feel this should be here. The game has a lot of grinding, you get to points in the level curve that you've completed all quests on both sides of the map and the next area is 10+ levels above you. You are forced to grind for 5-10 levels unless you've saved your EXP cards you get from questing to boost you through the curve and over to the exp reset. This can both be a pro and con since some people like the grind and some people hate it.

[h1]CONS:[/h1]
[list]
[*]No P2P trading for free users. Even Token is limited to 30 trades a month.
[*]Can't trade Silver (In-game general currency) through trading.
[*]Extremely limited AH, only 1 without a Token. Even with Token its limited to only 5 items for sale.
[*]AH is on a ridiculous timer to claim silver after an item is purchased. Nearly 2 days wait to retrieve most sales.
[*]AH takes a HUGE cut of profit, 30% might as well vendor the items unless they're worth 1mil+ even then you lose a ton. Token users get this reduced to (?15%?)
[*]Loot distribution is allocated to persons dealing highest amount of damage on every setting. Tested and confirmed, aprox ~90% of the time the person with highest damage gets loot. As an aoe wizard I clear groups and get most if not all loot over my friends in the party through-out the zone. Even on round-robin I had gotten 5 items before someone else got 1.
[*]Buffs are limited. Yes you heard that right, BUFFS are limited. There are skills that increase how many buffs you can have, and buffs that give you more... buff slots. Token users can have more buffs.
[*]Limited dungeon entries. You can't freely grind dungeons like, nearly, EVERY other MMORPG out there. For some reason its crazy bad if you can grind exp/loot in a dungeon, limit is 2 entries per day, 3 for Token users.
[*]Limited Global chat, or shout chat. You need to spend TP (In-game Cash Shop currency) to buy Megaphones to talk in global (shout). There is a pro to this as seen above though.
[*]Some of these limitations are to stop gold spammers/sellers (RMTers) but are completely useless since there are still hundreds of gold spammers per day. The only real thing the limitations do is destroy the multiplayer aspect of the game.
[*]Selected wrong class for advancement? Sucks to be you, make a new character, enjoy grinding to 200 again. You can buy a Skill Reset potion which will allow you to reset skill allocations, but not your chosen class advancement.
[*]Tokens CAN'T be given to people to allow them to become premium, since you can't trade to non-token players. Even if you could trade, Tokens can't be traded except for through the marketplace. ADDITIONALLY, only Tokens bought through TP (In-game Cash Shop currency) can actually be sold.
[*]Guilds can't be made unless you become a Templar class which is Swordsman ONLY access. As far as my own research has gone, you need select it for your 7th class advancement, which is pretty much end game, before you can even think about leading.
[*]Attribute training is limited to RESEARCHING 1 at a time, 2 for Token users. This can be confusing as the game says you can only learn 1 at a time, but it actually means you can only research 1 at a time. You can learn ALL attributes, it just takes time (and Silver).
[*]Enchanting a cosmetic costs an Enchanting Scroll from the TP Cash Shop. Enchanting is extremely RNG and you could waste $100 and not get anything worth anything.
[*]Collections can be complicated. You must first find a hidden chest (if there is one) in the Area you are to start a collection. Then you must collect misc material drops which can include rare accessory's and armor or weapons. Additionally, you must take the collection crate to allow the collection to an NPC in town. To complete the collection you need to put the items in the collection vendor which consumes them.
[*]Specific class restricted crafting. Some Classes (Archer/Wizard) have a special class advancement allowing them to craft special items. You must take that class over a DPS/Support class in order to make these items or buy them from someone who can.
[*]You must talk to a specific TP Cash Shop vendor to buy TP items. you need to plan ahead or risk needing to teleport back if you want to grab an item (Soul Stone, EXP tome, etc)
[*]When upgrading an item after X amout of upgrades you have a chance to fail and lose potential, after all potential is gone the item will be destroyed. Trading, team sharing, adding a gem socket, or buying an item from the AH causes the item to lose 1 potential instantly. 
[*]When using Team Storage you decrease item potential by 1 making trading items between characters just as bad as buying from the AH.
[/list]

[h1] Strongly recommend this for veteran MMORPG players [/h1]

[b][u]If you're in for a long, detailed read then proceed. That's just my writing style. If not then there's a TL;DR at the bottom.[/u][/b]

If you're a veteran MMORPG player from the golden age of MMORPG's, you've come to the right place. Tree of Savior is just about the only MMORPG to release in this decade that caters exactly to those that are fond of hardcore MMORPGs of an age long ago. The style, feel, input and feedback of the game pays much homage to MMORPG titles such as Ragnarok Online. In fact, the original director of Ragnarok Online is the director for this game. You can rest assured that this game will keep you busy with lots to do and much fun to be had.

Now let's get into the actual critic. This is actually my first review but I've played MMORPG's my entire life and have played this title for more than my actual listed play time.

PROS :

[list]
[*][b]Extreme[/b] class diversity 
[*][b]Unique[/b] class system
[*][b]Customizable stat distribution[/b]
[*]Rustic, nostalgic art style
[*]Amazing soundtrack 
[*]Hidden sub-quest lines
[*]Randomly generated events
[*]Support-type player friendly! 
[*]Boss monsters have attack patterns
[/list]

Alright. Let's put everything into context.

First and foremost is definitely the rustic feel of this game. The art style, atmosphere, music, everything just plays so well into constructing an amazing world for you to explore. The art style is extermely reminiscent of Ragnarok Online and some view Tree of Savior as the "true" sucessor to Ragnarok Online. You have all the amazing customizability and environment from Ragnarok Online put into a much more modern take on the same genre without losing it's original feel. 

The biggest attraction of Tree of Savior would definitely have to be the class system. Tree of Saviors class system is very unique in that a player can custom tailor their class to fit their specific play style. Are you a "Swordsman" class but prefer to use many new active skills instead of basic attacks? Advance into "Highlander" or "Barbarian" to progress down those paths and gain access to a whole new branch of skills. But maybe you enjoy using basic attacks. If that's the case, you can choose to further hone your skills as a "Swordsman" and invest further into your original first class instead of advancing into a "Highlander" or "Barbarian". Tree of Savior gives players the opportunity to "Rank up" their current class instead of advancing to a new class and increase the maximum skill levels of their current class' abilities, giving them potential to be stronger than those that followed a different path if utilized correctly.

Tree of Savior also encourages players to diversify their class choices to fit their play style. Just because you chose the path of a Wizard and advanced into a Pyromancer doesn't mean you're stuck being a flame based magic user forever. You can easily advance into a Cryomancer at the next class advance and become both! Just because you chose the path of magic doesn't mean your only role is damage dealing. You can advance into other classes that compliment your current set of skills as well. A Pyromancer has the ability "Flame Ground" which sets an area ablaze dealing Damage over Time. Should a Pyromancer also advance into a "Linker", a class that specializes in monster manipulation, the "Pyro-Linker" could set ground abalaze, "link" together monsters, and drag them over the fire to be slow roasted. There are plenty of classes with complimenting skills such as this example. The greatest thing about Tree of Savior is finding them all and trying them. 

Customizable stat distribution is a very big thing for me. It means that the game does not have a "preset" style of playing that the game has already defined for you. If you feel like being a warrior class that goes complete glass cannon and forsakes all durability put everything into Strength and have at it. If you feel like playing a Wizard up close and personal you can easily stat in some extra Vitality for some health. If you feel that you want to shoot arrows faster rather than harder, you can easily stat in Agility for some speed. Being able to customize your stat inputs helps you refine what your playstyle would be instead of just following along a guide.


Now onto the cons. A game without cons does not exist. But Tree of Savior has some debateable cons so let's get into them.

CONS:

[list]
[*]Linear Leveling system 
[*]Bizarre map layout
[*]Segregated maps
[*]Grind
[/list]


Tree of Savior players on a linear leveling system of starting at level 1, to infinity. That is to say, there is no level cap. In concept, this is designed so that players play at their own pace because there is no race to a "end game" goal to do content. Players will just play at their own leisure finishing content as they progress into different worlds and areas. However players must be reminded that this was originally a Korea MMORPG. It takes alot. [i]alot[/i]. Of grinding to progress speedily. In my humble opinion this is actually a good way to gate players from speeding through the entire games' content in a single week. But in a game whoms biggest emphasis is replayability by creating multiple characters in different classes, it just slows down progress a ton and doesn't feel great. Grind is both a necessity but a gimp when it comes to MMORPG designing. In all honesty comparatively to other MMORPG's, the grind isn't so bad but it is there nonetheless.

This may be a smaller point but the map layout for Tree of Savior is a bit strange. You'll be progressing linearely through the game and maps and everything will be placed within your level zone, but should you decide to explore a bit the map directly underneath your level 20 map could be a level 100+ map. Now the monsters won't instantly agro and oneshot you or anything, infact they won't agro you at all if you're out of the level gap, but it's just a bit strange unless you're the explorative type. Because of the linear map progression based on current level, you'll never really re-visit older maps save for farming specific materials or major towns and adjacent fields. 


My conclusion for this game is you should definitely try it. Whether you're an MMORPG Veteran or a newbie to the genre the experience playing it was amazing and you won't experience another game like it.

I really wanted to like this game. It's a throwback to what I enjoyed most about MMOs before everything became an amusement park with quest spam. The core gameplay and setup are great and I think it could have been one of the best MMO's out there, but its execution falls short.

I won’t go into the negatives on how the trading restrictions go with the token item, since this is what the devs thought might be a legitimate way to solve the bot/real-money-trading problems most MMOs have. I'll just say that in the end it did not work out and turned out to be a really bad decision that many players ended up disliking from the get-go.

The main reason why I cannot recommend this game starts here. When you first spawn in the game, this is where they hook you. There are tons of low level mobs in the starter areas that die within 1-2 hits. It’s very fun and satisfying to mow down monsters and watch them explode into pieces and collect the money and items they drop. When you think of a game where the core is to grind monsters to level up (along with quests of course), you would think that you’d be playing like this the whole way getting more challenging, but that setting changes drastically shortly after the first/second dungeon. Mob density gets extremely low and that fun atmosphere of destorying piles of creatures before you starts to become tedious. Imagine playing a high intensity action RPG game like Diablo II or III, and when you reach a higher level the mobs start to take more hits as they should, but instead of killing hoards of 30 skeletons they condense it down to 2 or 3 with experience getting shallower and shallower as you go. The only reason why I didn’t quit sooner is because dungeons fulfill this problem, with many mobs available and a good amount of strategy needed, it’s simply fun. But here's the real issue with dungeons, you have a global dungeon limit, so that fun is short lived. This might be okay for the average person who maybe spends about an hour in game, but for those who want to spend more time slaying, you're gonna have to wait.

The second main reason I cannot recommend this game is how the game runs. I've never complained about how a game runs before in my lfie, granted I have a nice system that usually runs most AAA 3D games on high/ultra, so it’s very sad to see a game with this art style and caliber run so poorly on so many systems. Alone it’s easy to hit 50-60 FPS while killing low density monsters, but when you get into dungeons with a full party of effects and more mobs on-screen, you can drop well below 25 FPS often. Towns also have the worst FPS drops due to the amount of players on screen at once. I purposfully look for channels with no players just so I can move around. I can only imagine the frustration of PVP with this lag. You know, I can deal with some ports having 30 FPS locked, but if your game goes below that during the core of gameplay, it's simply unacceptable.

There’s a ton of good stuff in this game. Like I said, the game feels fun to play when you don’t lag, especially in dungeons when there’s plenty to fight. The stat/class system is one of the most interesting out there, giving you lots of freedom to be whoever you want to be. I personally understand this would be hard to balance without lots of trial and error. You can buy buffs/upgrades/repairs from other players to make your leveling easier, which is neat if you want to solo for a bit and it’s an interesting way for other players to get money other than the normal MMO routes. Being able to teleport to finished quest NPC’s is great since it eliminates downtime. The art style and music for this game I should mention is top notch for fans of the genre like me. I should also mention that this game doesn't feel P2W at all (at the time of this review). If it is, it's the least I've ever felt in a FTP game ever. The community on Reddit is pretty cool too, as it really shows that people wanted this game to succeed. I did too.

At the end of the day, if the game isn’t fun as early as mid game due to the FPS/mob problem then what is going to keep players playing? I’m fine with it being a grind game, but you have to make the grind fun and you have to give players things to do (I didn’t touch end game since I’m not there, but it appears to be pretty shallow there too). If FFXIV can turn around their game, I think TreeOfSavior can too, but I highly doubt the devs would re-release this game after fixing it. If they did, I’d be interested, though I’m not holding my breath since the speed at which they make improvements we’d probably have Half-Life 4 and flying cars by then. It’s saddening to see so much potential thrown out the window, because they’ve built a very solid base, but sadly, it may already be too late.

[h1]Let me start by saying Tree of Savior has its flaws. They are as follows:[/h1]

[list]
[*][b][u]Problems with bots[/u][/b] which the development team is aware of. Already they have patched in a bot report system and I assume there are more fixes in the works.
[*][b][u]Bugs[/u][/b] which are plenty, however not game breaking. There are some oddities in the gameplay of some of my friends who have played where sprint does not function properly. There are cosmetic bugs to be found here and there, however I haven't found anything in my own experience of playing around 22 hours that was game breaking.
[*][b][u]Server lag[/u][/b] is probably the biggest issue with the game to-date. Even in its current state with only 'founder' access to the game there are many times when the servers are populated to the point of gameplay becoming affected. Sometimes lag is to the point where you can't kill an enemy until it settles down. One can only hope they do something to improve the performance of the servers.
[*][b][u]Framerate[/u][/b] can drop below 60fps in heavily populated areas even on a good computer. Running the game on a GTX 980 I did not expect to experience any visual lag in a game that emulates a 2.5D appearance. In the big cities of Orsha and Klaipeda though you will certainly drop below 60fps and see noticeable frame drops.
[*][strike][b][u]Fractured Community[/u][/b] on the server I play on, Orsha. While I have nothing against my brothers and sisters in Brazil, there are too many Portugeuse-only speakers on Orsha for an English-only speaker to become very invested in the community. While the title of the game on Steam says it is the English version of Tree of Savior, it is obvious that the Brazilian community deserves their own server.[/strike] 
[*][b][u]Free players can't do much[/u][/b] in the current version of ToS. You can't trade or put up more than 1 item on the marketplace at a time. Of course the developers need to make money...so for now this is their solution to incentivize buying premium for the game. The developers have said they are looking for a way to allow free players to trade, however you can't help but think it will be limited in some way. Only time will tell what economic decisions the devs will have to make with the game. Thus is the nature of F2P.
[*][b][u]Character customization[/u][/b] is weak. You can choose male or female, however there are limited options for both genders. 
[/list] 

[h1]So what is there to like about Tree of Savior?[/h1]

[list]
[*][b][u]Combat[/u][/b] is probably the biggest pro in Tree of Savior. The action combat in the game is satisfying. Every wave of enemies you kill feels like a blast of progression towards the next level. Each class in the game plays a unique style and takes advantage of spatial awareness in the action combat. Boss battles utilize this very same aspect of the game. If you see a boss charging up an attack, don't just stand and auto-attack, run!
[*][b][u]Controls[/u][/b] feel old-school and backwards at first [i](I mean arrow keys to control...what is this 1993?!)[/i], but once you understand how to access the game's different menus through your function keys and get familiar with moving around it all feels very intuitive. Even something as simple as teleporting to a completed quest is made easy with just a quick press of backspace. It's nice how almost everything in the game able to be controlled without lifting your hands from your keyboard.
[*][b][u]Visuals[/u][/b] are great in Tree of Savior. Everything is rendered in 3D, but the game is textured and lit in such a way that you could swear you're looking at the 2.5D Ragnarok Online. It's a beautiful effect, and it makes exploring more enjoyable. Each area in the game has a unique environment and flora. This is a game whose graphics have character. You will dangerously wander into higher level areas if you don't keep your eyes on the road. 
[*][b][u]Interface[/u][/b] is good. It is nothing revolutionary but everything is where you would expect it to be. All your menus are accessed through your function keys, F1-F12. This is unique for an MMO where 'I' is typically your inventory, 'E' will access your equipment, etc. It takes some time to get used to, but it's actually a relief with the action gameplay to have all your menu buttons out of the way of an accidental keystroke.
[*][b][u]Class diversity[/u][/b] is wide ranging. You can play any style you want with 80 possible class combinations. Some classes can advance to higher levels, or 'circles'. Some classes appear to have limited usefulness in the current version of the game, so do your research before dedicating yourself to a particular line of classes. That being said, no class is the wrong choice as long as you know what is and is not recommended for that particular class. Again, do some basic research on the many guides and manuals written by the community and make your own informed decision of how you want to play the game. [b]EDIT:[/b][i]A note on classes...while there are 80 different choices of classes in Tree of Savior, not all of them are a viable option. In fact, many of the circle 3 classes are weak and don't provide any useful skills. It is worthy to note as well that only one or two stats per class are really useful, for instance a swordsman player set on going Hoplite may allocate stats to only STR, STR and DEX, or STR and CON. At the end of the day whatever class you choose know that ToS is a game about damage and your choices have to reflect that to succeed. Many years ago, Tree of Savior set out to create a spiritual sequel to Ragnarok Online, a unique MMORPG I still hold in high regard, despite its many, many flaws.

The most striking feature of the game is the selection of 80+ classes, ranging from traditional to odd and quirky; the number is a little misleading, however, with each class only bringing around 7 abilities, and characters getting (at the time of writing) 8 opportunities to change their class (or unlock more abilities from an existing one) as they gain levels. The amount of potential skill builds and combinations this allows to create and experiment with is still quite impressive.

The grind also survived. You are expected to slaughter thousands of monsters to advance, most of which pose little threat and the focus is thus more on dealing with crowds. There are a lot of quests to boost your XP gains, but they rarely ask you to do anything more complex than slaughtering a specific type of monster or using a thing before you do so. Whether that helps break up the monotony of prevent that grinding trance depends on the player. They do, however, occasionally lead to boss fights and/or good rewards, so try to at least follow those orange main quests.

Unfortunately, the grind rarely pays off. Ragnarok made it rewarding through strong equipment identities — few things were “slightly better sword” because of unique bonuses and customisation opportunities. ToS replaces most of that with random equipment that can drop from nearly any monster in the appropriate level range, on par with or downright better than items that require hunting down specific enemies or resources. So far, I haven’t seen a truly unique or specialised item. At best whatever bonus it had would be obsoleted by the next level tier’s equipment. Speaking of equipment customisation, it can be straight-up upgraded, set with general-purpose coloured gems and specific monster gems. Those latter essentially replace monster cards, but their effect is limited to +1 to a particular skill, and they don’t even show up on all monsters. Not a lot of hats to find, either, which is a shame, because character customisation is limited to hats and a class-specific outfit.

Monster identities were another major part of Ragnarok — many were designed to be strong against one type of character, but weak to another, giving plenty of reasons to play with others — or at least start multiple characters. Even when elemental strengths and weaknesses came into play, I found myself not really trying to find monsters I have an advantage over. Furthermore, ToS introduces XP penalties based on the level difference, so you’re punished for trying to punch above your weight or staying in the same area too long.

Character attributes are, from what I understand, linear and don’t have that much of an impact. I managed to make it to level 170 (of 350+) without allocating anything; and then not noticing that much of a difference when I dumped nearly everything in my attack stat. Secondary attributes, like dexterity (critical hits) and constitution (HP maximum) may have a more pronounced effect, but without extensive testing, I cannot draw any conclusions. Respec potions are available through the real money store or the occasional event, should you want one.

The game attempts an action-based, direct control scheme, but the effort can hardly be called successful. Many classes have abilities that exploit or change positioning, and telegraphed attacks that can be physically dodged are somewhat common. Unfortunately, limited mobility, uncooperative target selection, fairly slow attacks, and good old lag issues make combat more clunky and less satisfying than it could be. Even basic navigation can be frustrating thanks to awkwardly high and short jumps, and inconsistent map passability.

If you’re looking for a story in your MMORPG, this one definitely isn’t it. It is present, and admittedly some quests offer decent stories, but the translation varies from barely legible to surprisingly good. Skill descriptions in particular are vague (and possibly outdated), so get ready to google.

Left outside the scope of this review are PvP and instanced dungeon experience, neither of which I have any interest in. I’m not quite to the highest levels yet, but I’ve never felt any pressure to try those, or even attempt to communicate with another player, playing a supposedly support character.

All in all, I find Tree of Savior very hard to recommend, unless you are nostalgic for Ragnarok Online. Even then, brace for disappointment. It doesn’t add enough to update RO for a modern audience, and removes too much to be a proper remake. In addition to that, the game is awfully optimised, happily consuming large amounts of GPU and CPU power even on the character select screen. Still, it is the closest we can get to either right now, it’s free, and it’s not completely pay-to-win.

Lots of people are comparing this game to Ragnarok Online (RO), but Tree of Savior is actually more similar to another famous IMC game, Granado Espada (GE). The same group of people worked on all three games, and it shows.

While its art and class design is meant to invoke RO, the teams system, item shop, megaphones, EXP cards, map design, audio, and even costumes are basically copied from GE.

[*]Unsuitable music. The throbbing techno was an good choice for the grimy world of GE, but not here. The RO soundtrack alternated between light ambiance and memorable themes, which would've suited ToS better.

[h1]The Misunderstood:[/h1]

[list]
[*]Questing may seem linear at first, but becomes more open world later on. The map progression system is identical to GE, but not fully open world like RO. 
[*]Grindy for a modern day MMO. Roughly as grindy as GE, but thankfully nowhere as grindy as RO. Some people like this, some people don't.
[*]The class system feels overwhelming at first, but it's designed to create highly specialized characters that provide a niche service to parties or the entire community (crafting, upgrading, etc). This is similar to RO, and indeed many skill concepts in ToS are borrowed from RO/GE. But due to the grinding, there needs to be easier/cheaper ways to reset characters. 
[/list]

[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]

As with RO and GE, Tree of Savior was created by a talented team with big ambitions, powerful artistic vision, but poor quality control. These are the type of creative folks who have great ideas, but don't know how to package or deliver their product professionally. This has resulted in rough launches and patchwork gameplay (especially questing) during the early days of all three games. 

That being said, RO and GE both went on to be very successful MMOs. If there is one thing that could doom ToS, it's the excessive restrictions for non-premium players.

Despite its shortcomings, the game is clearly a labor of love with much content to explore. If out of nothing but nostalgia, I would still recommend giving Tree of Savior a try.

Here is a long list of problems with Tree of Savior:

1) You can't trade with other players. You read it right! You can't trade at all. The only way to trade with your friend, is if both of you purchase a 18$ token that allows trading for 30 days. 3) You can only put 1 item in the auction house, the item takes a random time between 30 minutes and 2 hours to appear on the market, after you sell it there's 30% tax, and you need to wait over 2 days to retrieve silver from the market! If you have a token, you can put up 5 items at a time and the tax is reduced to 10%. There is another limitation to the market - the price at which you try to sell your item is adjusted by the system and there's nothing you can do about it.

4) IMC (game developer and publisher) did all of the trade/market restrictions supposedly to fight the RMT traders (goldsellers). It did absolutely nothing. Goldsellers are still littering the game. The real reason behind those changes was to force players to spend 18$ a month on a token.

5) As a result of the above, the market is a joke. If you enjoy a healthy marketplace, that's not what you'll find here. Playing the market to earn money is barely profitable because of the market's flaws. The market is bugged and can be exploited by malicious players.

6) You can't create a guild until you have reached rank 7, which is nearly the level cap of 280. For the whole game you can't be in a guild.

7) This game destroys the social aspects of interacting with other players. I'll make a short list:

a) When you make a party, you expect to be able to choose basic loot options. Not in this game. You can only choose Round Robin, Random or Pick-Up. If you play with random people, you can't trust them enough to have pick-up option enabled, because one of them will most likely steal all the loot. There is no class-restriction when looting, no dice-roll system, no greed/need system, no bid system like in B&S. Pray to RNJesus that you get the drops that you need.

b) When you're leveling with a friend, you can't trade without a Token. Even if you buy that, you will be restricted to 30 trades per month. You'll run out of this limit in a week of playing together.

c) Market has so many limitations, it destroys the idea of healthy and vibrant economy. In this game, you'll think twice before putting anything on sale.

d) All the leveling/questing is easily soloable. An MMORPG is supposed to be a multiplayer game, where people feel the need to party up to clear the hard content. Here, the only times you'll need a party is for dungeons or for grinding spots that are heavily contested for.

e) The mob population is too small, there are not enough mobs for everyone on the map. There are not enough channels to accomodate all people. The spawn timer is between 2-5 minutes for almost all mobs! So 80% of the time, instead of fighting, you'll be running around trying to find mobs to kill.

f) Dungeons have a limit entry of 2 times per day. And this limit entry is shared between all dungeons. So, if you do dungeon A 2 times today, you can't enter dungeon B or C. If you have a token, that's 3 entries per day.

g) You can't queue to a dungeon if you're in a party. If you enter a dungeon in a pre-made party, you only get 450% exp bonus. If you queue solo, you get 600% bonus. You either go with people you know and get punished for that, or you queue with random people who probably have no idea how to play.

f) Same thing with PvP - you can't queue if you made a premade party. Want to play PvP together with a friend? Sorry, you can't.

8) The game is, not very advanced in terms of graphical effects and shouldn't be very demanding on your PC. At least in theory. You'll need a high-end PC to enjoy a framerate exceeding 50 fps.

9) You will be getting random screen stuttering all the time. If you play in a party, sound begins to stutter when 5 people are hitting one boss at the same time. It's painful to hear.

10) Dungeons give way too much exp. Consequently, many players will just do their daily runs and log off because grinding on the fields isn't very efficient exp-wise.

11) The issues with lag/latency/server instability are very bad. I've played many MMORPG in the past, some of them right from day 1, but never experienced something like this. On the first day, the only way to login was to select a server, click "Enter" button, then patiently wait for 2-3 minutes to log in. If during that time, you clicked "Enter" button again, you are put right at the end of the queue. There was no way of figuring it out that you're supposed to wait patiently for 2-3 minutes to log in. Most players would just assume that the login is broken and keep clicking on the "Enter" button every few seconds. 
If you managed to log in, there were queues everywhere, that could take up to 2 hours or more. It persisted for more than 2 days. The lag during combat was tolerable. But, the lag manifests if you want to talk to NPCs or use an item. You can't even pick-up drops from mobs instantly, it takes over 10 seconds for them to be picked up. When walking around, you will be randomly teleported back because of the server issues.

12) There is little to none communication with IMC or their Staff. They don't respond to people constantly complaining about the problems I mention in this review. Some of those problems have existed in the game since the first closed beta, but still weren't fixed. Some of the quests, mobs and NPCs are bugged since over 6 months ago, and guess what? It's never been fixed.

13) The game is tending towards being a cash-grab product. You are blocked from basic functions like trading with other players if you don't pay. In KR, you need to spend TP (real-cash currency) to list items in the auction house. Buying a hair costume costs 20$. You can't trade items between your main and alts unless you have a Token. There is already P2W item in the shop that gives random stat bonuses to accessories, and this game was just recently released. Despite the players' reaction in KR and overseas, they will probably keep bringing more P2W items in the future.

There are only 6 costumes in total right now. The hair costumes are overpriced, and it costs way more to buy a female hair than male hair, which is a ridiculous cash grab.

A beautiful game with a unique art style and influences, and a painstaking amount of effort and creativity put into its maps, classes, and bizarre host of monsters. It sells its visuals almost purely on the quality of the storybook-esque hand drawn art, mixing sprites and 3D models seamlessly in a fixed perspective, building a visual style all its own without chasing photorealism. 

The music is also an absolute triumph, with a quality soundtrack more than a hundred songs broad. Every environment has not only its own leitmotif, but its own *playlist* of motifs, 3-5 tracks long. 

The minute to minute gameplay is satisfying and reasonably deep, with big active skill lists, short cooldowns, and manually aimed attacks eschewing the target-based systems of past MMO's like Ragnarok. The greater gameplay loop is fairly set in stone, however, without too much extra to do beyond the crazy storyline, dungeons, GvG, seasonal events, and daily queued activities.

ToS's class system is an interesting proposition for anyone interested in building both unique and well-optimized characters, and offers a lot of freedom to do unusual things, though for its incredible breadth it pays in being unevenly balanced. Still, what can one really expect when classes exist whose entire set of skills is solely magical wood-carving, kabbalah, or falconry? 

But honestly? Here's the real reason I play Tree of Savior: it's made by developers who care. 

Not about you; not personally. Other reviews will back me there: IMC is a Korean company, and the language and distance barrier is real. But they're unlike any other developer I've ever known, Korean or otherwise: they legitimately care about what it is they're doing, beyond the point of obligation, and have the power to see it done.

ToS is long past its initial surge of popularity, but it sees frequent and regular updates in every aspect - UI, core systems, classes, areas, dungeons, graphics, sound. Every few months there's something new, and something old has been refined to work a little better. IMC blunders often, at times almost comically naive or misguided in its intentions (yet never malicious) - but it self-examines, adapts, and corrects itself in ways I'd never thought plausible. It does something I've never seen before in a professional dev studio: it takes fault and then it actually fixes what's wrong. 

This is a developer who envisioned a classic paywall MMO, asked the world what it wanted, rolled out a F2P beta instead which granted earlier access in increments to supporters who paid more, and within a week retooled everything to a simple formula of "any donation = early access" in response to the (fully justified) displeasure of its players. This is a developer who nearly a year into release undertook a complete rebalancing of every skill, class, and weapon to address balance and playability concerns. These are the people who keep a running, up-to-date blog on their official site that talks honestly about issues in its core design and the studio's plans for fixing them.

There's no profit in this; ToS itself may not even be a particularly profitable endeavor in 2017, though I sincerely hope it's at least holding steady. But they keep at it, because it's the game they want to make. Because it's their pride and joy, and they care about it more than anyone.

Simply put, Tree of Savior is fun as hell and it isn't a clone of World of Warcraft.

Now then, allow me to elaborate.

First of all, the music is phenomenal. The tracks are well composed, diverse, and beautiful. If that isn't enough, each area generally has multiple tracks so that you aren't listening to one song on repeat which is a really nice touch that most developers overlook.

Secondly, the graphics. While not hyper realistic or over the top, the graphics of Tree of Saviour are an interesting blend of 2D sprite components and 3D cell shading that create a gorgeous artistic style that can still be run by lower end machines.

Next, even at low levels, your skills feel powerful. Your moves have nice flashy animations that are impressive, and monsters explode on death making huge group kills ever so satisfying. Bosses are fun and interesting, scaling in challenge as you level up and progress through the story.

Moving on, the questing experience is different from other games. The NPCs that provide you with side-quests are often unmarked, so for the first time in a game in years I found myself talking to all the NPCs in an area. I learned about my surroundings, found a ton of extra quests, and enjoyed the exploration / interaction aspect that this deisgn choice creates. I do understand though that this aspect of the game isn't for everyone, so it is definitely something to be aware of.

The Cash Shop is purely costume and convenience items and steers clear of a Pay to Win environment. In fact, most of the Cash Shop items that matter at all are tradeable like the Premium Token, Tree of Savior's subscription equivalent.

Character customization may seem scare at character creation, but when you realize that the vast majority of the character customization options are both toggleable and available from the Market, Achievements, and the Class System, the lack of options during Charaction Creation kind of ceases to matter.

The Class and Statistic Systems are intense. There are over 80 Classes in the game and there are a boat load of combinations that you can build. You assign your stat points too, giving you complete control over your character.

The amount of options you have to control your character are fantastic. Want to use a Keyboard to do everything? You can. Not a fan of Keyboards and want to use your Mouse for everything? You can do that too. You like kicking it old school and want to lean back and use a Controller? Well, that's also an option. Want to switch between them? The game will just swap on the fly. You could drop your Controller and break it mid boss fight, and just start playing with the Keyboard if you knew your keybinds. That's awesome, cause Mouse and Controller batteries always seem to die at the worst times.

Finally, if you played the original Ragnarok Online, Tree of Savior feels like coming back to your house from an extended vacation. Things are familiar, you have to get used to them again, but above all, you're back home.

I would highly recommend this game. Haters gonna hate, I'm gonna play Tree of Savior.

Thanks for reading! Have a good one, and if you're gaming, may all your loots be phat!

I spent a very large amount of time on this game and I can say without a doubt, I do not recommend this to players. I listed pros and cons at the top with a brief explanation based on my own experience. Keep in mind I am a primarily pve player so my opinions on pvp are based on what I heard from friends and players in-game. I had 16 characters and 4 pets, 3 characters at rank 8, 7 at rank 7 and the other 6 at rank 5.

Pros:
[*]Pretty neat and cute, typical anime-style mmorpg aesthetic. There a lot of panty-flashing swordsman and archer classes if that's your thing (personally it's a turnoff for me)
[*]The art style of the npc portraits unique, with exaggerated proportions on most
[*]Large variety of class builds with the unique class system (also a con)
[*]Some classes have neat interactions with each other, such as ice railgun from Cryomancer's Ice Wall and Monk's Energy Blast. Or the skill of Dragoon 2 to double the physical attacks done to a monster through a debuff
[*]A large majority of Cash Shop items (including premium tokens and costumes) are purchaseable from other players with in-game silver
[*]Every 4 hours you accumulate 1 free tp (cash shop currency) to a max capacity of 5 free tp, so you can purchase cheap cash shop items (megaphones and revive crystals) each day
[*]An ok amount of events to help the players, ex. leveling tomes, gem abrasives to improve gems to improve gear, sometimes tp
[*]The first time you experience bosses can be exciting, especially world and field bosses which can take many players to kill depending on the level
[*]It's not standard point and click gameplay. Blocking, walking out of AoEs, action-type gameplay

Cons:
[*]This game is VERY POORLY OPTIMIZED. Even if you have a high end machine do not expect to play the game at 60+ fps all the time, IMC stated over a month ago an optimization patch was on the way but it still has not come yet
[*]There are a large amount of bugs that go on for weeks, or even a month or two without fixing, such as game-breaking ones like friends list crashing game or questing in a party getting you stuck (this one was fixed)
[*]Content updates are extremely sparse especially compared to the Korean version. We get their ui fixes before any content always
[*]Your looks are based on your class choice costumes, weapon, sub-weapon/shield, hats, and hair. Finer things such as eye lenses, some hair dye and expensive hair styles are cash shop only
[*]You need a Token \ premium status to access ACCOUNT and silver storage, get 0 cooldown on attribute training, gain one extra run for daily dungeons and one extra reroll for cubes (The main source of rare gear)
[*]*Having a large variety of possible class builds means that there are a ton of terrible to lackluster builds out there
[*]You start with 4 character slots, if you want to explore builds you need to keep buying character slots 
[*]Pets also take up a slot so you need even more slots if you're using a pet class
[*]There is currently a gacha system in the game, as of this moment I would not consider it pay to win, however it could go that way whenever the contents of it switch every 2 weeks
[*]Premium outfits used to be able to be directly bought out of the cash shop and now they are locked behind the medal store which requires you to exchange gacha items for medals
[*]A ton of reused models, textures, recolored enemies, reused bosses but with more hp, from levels 1-280. Variety finally pops up at 280+ content
[*]The difficulty in this game feels artificial. Instead of giving monsters new moves to use, all the recolored higher level monsters are just given a enormous hp boost or enough defense or magic defense to render attacks useless
[*]*Pvp is largely unbalanced, only solo queue is possible so you cannot play with your friends on Team Battle League
[*]Depending on which server and region you play, the population could be absolutely terrible

Good or Bad? You decide:
[*]To a certain extent you can solo your way to rank 7 via questing, after that you either need to do daily missions for a long time or grind in a group. At rank 8 it is no longer an option for most classes
[*]Guilds require a rank 7 class to create with a current maximum of 35 members in a guild at the moment, leading to a few powerful guilds and a lot of inconsequential ones
[*]PvP is directly linked to PvE, your gear matters, and doing pvp won't get you better gear, only abrasives to improve gems for gear
[*]The game never evolves from "kill stuff, ok kill stuff within time limit, ok defend this thing now" even in the endgame dungeon Earth Tower
[*]The game is not finished yet, the rumor is that there are going to be 10 ranks of classes with a supposed level cap of 600 (330 and 8 ranks right now) and continued introduction of hidden classes


*Regarding class choices, because of the large variety of classes, there is also a huge chance for making a mistake for your class choices. You cannot undo your class choices without restarting your character. There are a few classes that end up with dead ends such as Corsair 3, without logical and good choice for the next class at rank 8 to take. There are also classes such as Highlander and Featherfoot who have their DPS literally cut in half because some of skills dps only work with certain kind of monsters. There are some straight up broken classes such as Sadhu which can cause a desync bug. Or flat out ineffective classes such as Sadhu again because their main damage skill can be interrupted by a single attack. There are support classes whose function is only to be a repair shop or buff shop. And then there are overpowered classes such as Plague Doctor which has a skill that lets allies ignore rank 2 debuffs.
In PvP some class choices completely invalidate others. Such as Plague Doctor's Bloodletting completely shutting down all Wugushi's poisons. Or Sage's Missile Hole blocking all ranged and magic attacks. 

The Steam version is the International version containing 2 servers for North America, 1 for South America, 2 for South East Asia, and 1 for Europe. Obviously where the company is based (Korea) they get the latest updates first, Japan second, and International last. The amount of disaprity between our versions is huge. Despite a few months ago a huge update to the system to allow patches from the Korean version of Tree of Savior to come faster to our version, we are still 1-2 months behind. For some reason IMC has been extremely hesitant to port over actual gameplay and content patches to our version, instead favoring cash shop updates and minor UI improvements.


All the fun I had in the game was in experiencing different classes. The first time experiencing some monsters was fun, but after that the game just didn't have any substance other than the class system to me.

And with that I'll leave you a checklist whether or not you should play the game:
[*]Are you okay with artificial difficulty?
[*]Are you able to invest time in the game to earn a premium token through silver if you cannot afford one with money?
[*]Are you willing to reroll a character if you make a fatal class mistake?
[*]Will you be able to stick with your goal despite it being stagnant for months? (PvE, PvP, GvG)
[*]If you play with friends, are they devoted enough to play with you?
[*]If you reach the "endgame" will you be okay with waiting months before getting actual content updates?

If yes to all, give it a try, and I wish you good luck.

Ragnarok Online was my childhood game, when I found out about the release of this game I immediately bought the highest priced Founder Access without a second thought... after 2 weeks I immediately regretted my action.

1. Trade restrictions in this game is one of the most ridiculous one I've seen in my 15 years of gaming experiences, for the very reason that it is the first of its kind which actually caused trouble for my progression in-game as I tried to transfer materials from my main character to alternate (through storage slot temporarily enabled by premium subscription) only to find that some part of my materials are unable to transfer across. To make things worse, I then realized that it was now impossible for me to transfer back the materials from my alternate to my main. The game developer has justified their poorly implemented restrictions for the glorious purpose of stopping bots and gold sellers, and yet I see endless numbers of gold sellers bot-spamming ads in the main town everyday and bots running rampant in popular dungeons.

2. Unreasonably, or I should say, utterly stupid loot system with ridiculous drop rates for some items will make you totally feel like quitting the game at days when RNG doesn't work in your favour. To craft a mid-game equipment, the recipe required me to farm for 15 materials from a group of extremely weak monsters who spawn in very few numbers. Coupling with the fact that the drop rate for the said material is 0.75%, and general low spawn rate of certain monsters including this one, I have in fact attempted to farm for the material for hours and didn't get any at all. 

3. While this game succeeded in emulating the fun experiences of old school mmorpgs, they have unfortunately also retained features from the past which are obsolete and unacceptable in modern mmorpgs. Not only that, they have also incorporated some of the most despised features of a modern mmorpgs - a premium subscription option which treats non-premium players like worthless garbage with further restrictions (such as no item transfer between characters of the same account) on top of the abundance of restrictions already in existence. 

4. Server lag and instability, I don't even have to mention much here. 

The game, being spirit successor of Ragnarok Online, attempted to emulate the "old school" mmorpg format which many old fans including me really appreciated it much. Unfortunately many of the features from the older mmorpgs have become reprehensible in modern games such as the idea of making people grind for items with drop rate as low as 0.01%  from monsters which are slow to spawn and yield no exp gains. Worst of all, they have placed unreasonable restrictions on trading which would have helped to relax the overly stressful grinding of loots, for the very purpose which they still fail to achieve at the end of the day.
